prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin across all change types; at least 2 tests of a kind are required to establish a rule.
Evidence is still thin for adoption new_screen changes (only 1 test, which performed worse at -4.2% after noise correction).
Evidence is still thin for finish new_screen changes (only 1 test, which showed no clear effect at +1.4% after noise correction).
Predictions were too high for adoption new_screen (+10.0% predicted vs. -4.2% measured after noise correction).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_screen: -4.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Defer Sign-In After Pet Selection: Move the sign-in step to occur after pet selection so users choose their desktop pet before committing to creating or signing into an account. (why: Sign-in conversion is 72.9% and adoption conversion is 60.9%; letting users select their companion pet first builds emotional investment before requesting account authentication.)
1: [home, redesign] Redesign Waiting Screen with Progress Stage: Redesign the waiting screen into a stage layout featuring live progress tracking, generation status details, and estimated time remaining. (why: The home waiting step has a 201s median and 2336s mean duration, causing user drop-off while waiting for pet creation without clear feedback.)
2: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Display Diagnostic Flow: Add a display verification checklist step on the finish screen to check rendering permissions and confirm desktop pet visibility. (why: Support received 3 reports of pets failing to show up on desktop or app not opening, and the finish step conversion is low at 64.8%.)
3: [home, wait_info] Pet Generation Time Estimate & Notification Alert: Show an estimated wait time and allow users to toggle background notifications when pet generation completes. (why: The waiting screen has a very long mean duration (2336s), causing users to close or abandon the app assuming it is stuck.)
4: [adoption, copy] Photo Upload Quality Guidance: Add clear photo requirement copy and tips to the upload screen to guide users on high-quality pet photo selection. (why: Support received 3 emails about custom pet creation failing or looking wrong, and adoption conversion is low (60.9%).)
5: [sign_in, notification] Account Sync & Cloud Save Assurance: Show a notification banner on sign-in clarifying that account login backs up pet data and enables recovery across re-installs. (why: 8 support emails (the top support theme) complained about pets missing or reset after signing in again.)

scores.note: Funnel shows sign-in and adoption drop-offs, but no direct support email evidence for reordering.
High wait time in funnel points to problem, but full redesign requires new screens.
Both funnel and support emails highlight this, but new screen additions historically showed negligible lift.
Addresses long wait time duration in funnel, though support mail is silent on it.
Both funnel and 3 support emails point to upload issues; low-cost copy change.
Addresses top support complaint (8 emails) and sign-in drop-off with simple reassurance banner.
